newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent falls after bearish APIs, Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent falls after bearish APIs, Iraq news.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures fell back sharply after the market opened following the overnight release of bearish U.S. inventory data and news that Iraq was a step closer to resuming humanitarian oil exports.
August Brent crude was 20 cents a barrel weaker at 0930 GMT and stood at $18.17. July gas oil was 50 cents a tonne off at $162.50.
"The APIs have taken us down here and the news from Iraq has just confirmed for us that things are a little bit easier," one broker said.

Dealers were worried about stock data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) which showed a 4.7 million barrel build in crude stocks, against earlier expectations of a draw of 2.5 million barrels, while gasoline stocks fell by just 137,000 barrels compared with earlier expectations of 1.5 million.
Charles Gray at Prudential-Bache Futures said the impact of the API data could be short-lived, however, in the context of a tight situation in the physical markets in Europe.

"We are waiting to see what the shelf-life of this reaction to the APIs is," he said. "Wait and see if the U.S. brings more downwards pressure on the market, and if it seems that there is an erosion of this downwards momentum, then we could see this thing pick up a bit."

Iraq's U.N. coordinator, Staffan de Mistura, said on Wednesday the world body had received a preliminary draft of food procurement and distribution plans, bringing the country a step closer to resuming oil exports under an $2 billion oil-for-food deal.
De Mistura said he needed further meetings with Iraqi officials to fill in the gaps in the draft and added the U.N. had no objections to Iraq resuming oil sales at any time.
